summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, diabetes, migraines, obstructive sleep apnea, and a VP shunt was admitted for evaluation of atypical chest pain. Initial concern for acute coronary syndrome was ruled out by normal troponins, a negative CT angiogram for dissection or pulmonary embolism, and a stress test showing no perfusion defects. The chest pain was deemed non-cardiac, likely related to GERD, though it only partially responded to usual treatments and required morphine for relief. Her headache was consistent with her known migraines and improved with oxycodone, though narcotics were later discontinued due to dizziness likely related to BPPV and medication side effects. Blood pressure was managed by stopping atenolol and nifedipine due to orthostatic changes, continuing other antihypertensives. Diabetes was noted to be poorly controlled with persistent hyperglycemia; metformin was increased at discharge. She was counseled on smoking cessation and CPAP use, and discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.
